import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_36/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_36/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_36/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_36/training_3.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source3_36_1 and Source3_36_2 on 'County'
intermediate_step1 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="County", how="outer")

# Step 2: Join Source3_36_0 and Source3_36_1 on 'County'
intermediate_step2 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="County", how="outer")

# The final target schema is ['County', 'm1401', 'm1403']
# We want to produce Target3_36 with these columns.

# The best source for m1401 and m1403 combined is intermediate_step1 (joined Source1 and Source2)
# intermediate_step1 has columns: County, m1401, m1403

# intermediate_step2 has m1402 and m1401, but m1402 is not needed in target.

# We want to produce a table with all counties from all sources (including Source3 which only has County),
# but target examples show only counties that appear in the joined data with m1401 and m1403.

# To maximize coverage, we will:
# - Start from intermediate_step1 (County, m1401, m1403)
# - Left join intermediate_step2 (County, m1402, m1401) to get m1402 if needed (not needed here)
# - Since m1402 is not in target, ignore it.
# - Use intermediate_step1 as base, but fill missing m1401 from intermediate_step2 if any
# - Also, ensure all counties from Source3 are included (some counties may be missing in intermediate_step1)
# - For counties missing in intermediate_step1, try to fill m1401 and m1403 from intermediate_step2 and Source2 respectively.

# Prepare a DataFrame with all unique counties from all sources
all_counties = pd.Series(pd.concat([source0['County'], source1['County'], source2['County'], source3['County']])).drop_duplicates().reset_index(drop=True)
all_counties_df = pd.DataFrame({'County': all_counties})

# Merge intermediate_step1 (County, m1401, m1403) onto all_counties
df = pd.merge(all_counties_df, intermediate_step1, on='County', how='left')

# Merge intermediate_step2 (County, m1402, m1401) to fill missing m1401 if any
df = pd.merge(df, intermediate_step2[['County', 'm1401']], on='County', how='left', suffixes=('', '_from_step2'))

# Fill missing m1401 in df from m1401_from_step2
df['m1401'] = df['m1401'].combine_first(df['m1401_from_step2'])

# Drop the helper column
df.drop(columns=['m1401_from_step2'], inplace=True)

# For m1403, if missing, try to fill from source2 directly (County, m1403)
df = pd.merge(df, source2[['County', 'm1403']], on='County', how='left', suffixes=('', '_from_source2'))

df['m1403'] = df['m1403'].combine_first(df['m1403_from_source2'])
df.drop(columns=['m1403_from_source2'], inplace=True)

# Now, ensure columns are strings and keep the target schema order
df = df[['County', 'm1401', 'm1403']]

# Replace any missing values with 'NR' to match source data style
df['m1401'] = df['m1401'].fillna('NR')
df['m1403'] = df['m1403'].fillna('NR')

# Sort by County alphabetically to have consistent output (optional)
df = df.sort_values('County').reset_index(drop=True)

# Write the final target table to the specified path
df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_36/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

# Read source files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_36/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_36/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_36/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_36/training_3.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source0 and Source1 on County
joined_01 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="County", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source2 on County
joined_012 = pd.merge(joined_01, source2, on="County", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3 on County
final_join = pd.merge(joined_012, source3, on="County", how="inner")

# Select only columns in target schema: ['County', 'm1401', 'm1403']
# m1402 is not in target schema, so drop it
final = final_join[["County", "m1401", "m1403"]]

# Group by County to ensure uniqueness and match target keys
final = final.groupby("County", as_index=False).first()

# Write output to target file
final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_36/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
